selector.champion: Drug-induced dermatomyositis secondary to ipilimumab therapy
selector.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, and the symptoms recurred and worsened after a second course of ipilimumab, which supports the diagnosis of drug-induced dermatomyositis secondary to ipilimumab therapy. The presence of prominent erythema at nailfolds with dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results do not strongly support this diagnosis, and the presence of skin symptoms is more consistent with dermatomyositis

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced dermatitis
rejected.why: While the patient did develop skin symptoms after ipilimumab treatment, the presence of muscle weakness and other systemic symptoms suggests a more complex diagnosis than simple dermatitis

rejected.label: Lupus-like syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not strongly support this diagnosis, and the presence of a clear temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and symptom onset suggests a drug-induced condition

registry.preferred_name: Drug-induced dermatomyositis secondary to ipilimumab therapy
support_spans: Within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, she developed skin symptoms
After initial improvement and later disease recurrence, she received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later, which led to recurrence and worsening of symptoms
Prominent erythema at nailfolds with dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Grade 4/5 strength on resisted abduction of shoulders bilaterally
contradict_spans: Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers without evidence of inflammatory myositis (note: performed after corticosteroid treatment)
